ranked.name: HS1: feed-surface history view (the history slice from Avito's 'model 5')
ranked.lens: The data owner's own production L3 ranker, Avito 'model 5' (habr.com/ru/companies/avito/articles/1090584, Oct 2026; verified in reports/deep_ru_competitions.md TL;DR 1). Its candidates attend to a history FILTERED to target-surface actions (at most 50 events, plain views removed). It beat a ~200-feature CatBoost by +7.2% NDCG, and Avito blends the two 1:1 by rank. So the heterogeneous strong member comes from a different history VIEW, not a different architecture. OTTO and H&M teams likewise built models on different event subsets or windows (reports/deep_otto_hm.md:193, where two-week models alone gave an 'only slight' gain). Mapping to our data: our target is an engagement started from the feed (source s1; CODES_DECODING §0.3), so the label-aligned slice is the s1 events. Not in COVERAGE_MAP.
reasons:
ok: Not refuted. No COVERAGE_MAP or registry row uses the same mechanism: the s1-only view applied to every GPU-side history channel has not been tried.
- hcap (COVERAGE_MAP wave-4) caps event types for format parity, in the cooldown only.
- HDROP-ALL thins events at random and averages back with TTA.
- r6 Q2 'typed' (EXPERIMENT_REGISTRY:71; nn_x/r6/logs/r6_eval_screen_a4u_wd01_cset_typed_adrop0_a4w.txt:87: +0.00043 val, rho_x 0.9783 vs rho_bb 0.9784) sliced only the last cross block, to e1&s1 events, and kept the full history everywhere else.
- AUDIT_1112 §4.6 and CODES_EXPLOIT tested source cues as residual features, not as a member view.
- EXTERNAL_TOP1 D3 was never run.

Three supporting claims contradict recorded facts. They lower the prior; they do not void the idea.

(1) The Avito precedent is misread. deep_ru_competitions.md:71/297 and EXTERNAL_TOP1_1113.md:146/220 say model 5 filters by ACTION TYPE: target actions (contacts and favourites), clicks excluded. It also keeps the recs, search and external sources as per-event embeddings. HS1 does nearly the inverse. Per CODES_DECODING §2 'Scope', a source is set only for e1/e4/e7; e2/e3/e5/e6/e8/e9/e10 are always s0. So HS1 keeps mostly feed card views and drops every contact and delivery event. The production precedent does not transfer.

(2) HS1 is not a 'view swap'. The base already sees the source of every event: model.py forward `self.es(b["hes"])`, the retrieval value term `e_src`, and AUDIT_1112 §4.6 'the history encoder already has type + source tokens per event'. The s1 view is a strict subset of the base's information, so HS1 is an information removal. On the brief's own frontier, removals land at about 4:1 (no_retr, ctx_nd, pre2), and pop-free is about 6:1. The pop-free family is the precedent for removal used as diversity: member corr 0.933-0.938, member val -0.0025 / holdout -0.0081, G3+family H -0.00052 (z -2.45) (CURRENT_STATUS 06:09/06:39). To reach +0.005 margin within -0.0010 val, HS1 must sit off that frontier.

(3) Further evidence weighs against strength:
- AUDIT §4.6 gives lift 0.91 for categories seen only via search vs 0.52 for 'neither'. HS1 merges these two cases in the per-category counts.
- Typed's +0.00043 says nothing about strength without the full history, because typed kept it.
- slicefeat.py skips feeds with an empty s1 slice before computing AUC, so the 0.636 vs 0.643 comparison leaves out the 2.1% of feeds where HS1 can rank only at chance.

There is also a spec gap that would corrupt the readout. holdout_eval.py:23 and stale_pred.py:60 rebuild SplitData with no view. As written, the holdout and stale-val predictions would be scored on the full history, a train/inference mismatch.

Priors: P(same strength) ~0.25; P(member corr <= 0.92) ~0.1 (the frontier says it comes with a cost); P(both, and the pool moves) ~0.03. | fix: (a) Drop the Avito model-5 justification, or test its actual filter (e2/e3/e4/e7/e9 from any source, views excluded) as a second arm. HS1 is close to the inverse of model 5 and removes every contact event.

(b) Apply the view wherever SplitData is built, driven by the checkpoint's args (ck['args']['hist_src']) rather than a separate CLI flag:
- train.py: tr/va/te;
- finetune.py:125-134: va/te/trd;
- holdout_eval.py:23;
- stale_pred.py:60.
Add a test that the holdout predictions from holdout_eval.py equal train.py's selection-holdout predictions for an HS1 checkpoint.

(c) Before the 10-epoch pair, run a ~1 GPU-h 2-epoch screen in the nn_x/abl harness (seeds 23/24 vs the abl base), the same setting in which the 4:1 removal frontier was measured. Pre-declare: the pair proceeds only if 2-epoch member val >= -0.0015, (rho_bb - rho_x) / |dval| >= 5, and rho_bb - rho_x >= 0.005 at that length. Otherwise CLOSED as 'removal on the frontier'.

(d) Recompute the slicefeat AUC with empty-s1 feeds scored at chance, and report how much of the 2.1% empty-slice share falls in guest feeds and M<50 feeds. Those slices are vetoes in the rule.

ok: I'm not refuting HS1. No COVERAGE_MAP row covers the same mechanism and there is no leak: the slice is the feed's own as-of history, it uses no labels, and holdout selection depends only on p_random and M. Nothing recorded contradicts it either. But my CPU checks show its prior is low, and that the 0.92 member-correlation target is almost certainly out of reach.

1) The shared history component is mostly NOT on the GPU side. Check (scratchpad/hs1_skeptic/sig_load.py, val, 1.39M rows). Signal = z-mean of w5_e10_base_s951-954. Within-feed correlation of the signal with each cue:
- pre2_hmax32, an xt input (max similarity over the FULL history from the pre-trained encoder): 0.607
- smax(full), GPU side: 0.602
- smax(s1): 0.580
- ctx_nd_knn_h, xt: 0.465
HS1 keeps all of these xt inputs as they are. In a within-feed regression of the signal:
- cos_u + 5 xt inputs alone: R2 0.459
- adding smax_full: 0.490
- using smax_s1 instead: 0.487
- partial loading on smax_full: 0.27
The first-order swap gives a signal correlation of 0.990 (0.981 for the fitted linear part).

2) Label-level check (scratchpad/hs1_skeptic/label_proxy.py): a linear ranker, 2-fold user-grouped, with 16 xt/f inputs. NDCG:
- full-history smax/lse/top3: 0.36676
- s1-slice: 0.36652 (-0.00024 +- 0.00028)
- no GPU-side cue at all: 0.36626
The full and s1 rankers correlate 0.9953. The slice is cheap for the same reason it barely decorrelates: the xt inputs already carry the full-history similarity. Any real decorrelation would have to come from the learned retrieval and attention channel. That channel's removal (no_retr) sits on the proposer's own 4:1 frontier: margin 0.014 at -0.0034.

3) Implied numbers. Base members correlate 0.9475 with each other, so an HS1 member would correlate about 0.9475 x (0.981-0.995) = 0.93-0.943 with a base member, not <= 0.92. The pool margin would be about 0.974 x (0.005-0.019) = 0.005-0.018, so the D clause can be met, but only at the margins where 2-member pools have lost before. Examples (pool-level diversity margin): e30 0.0066, bs4 0.0098, bs4lr4 0.0053; all three pools were still negative. Families with a different view but weaker members also lose val in the pool: in decide4_interim_1350, adding F10 (GRU) to F7x+F7x70 changed val by -0.0006 and holdout by +0.0002.

4) Closest prior run. The r6 typed arm used the same e1&s1 filter in the last cross block: val +0.00043, holdout +0.00020, rho_x 0.9783 vs rho_bb 0.9784, so no diversity. HS1 extends the slice to the dense cues, retrieval and the encoder, and that part is untested.

5) Data facts the spec should correct:
- Empty-slice share is 2.97% of val, 2.37% of test and 2.87% of train feeds, not 2.1%; of these, 1.35%, 0.86% and 1.12% are already empty in the full history.
- The s1 share of events is 0.376 on train vs 0.338 on val and 0.343 on test.
- PSI of the s1 count: 0.217 train->val and 0.211 train->test, vs 0.040 for the full H. That is below the 0.5 bar but a 5x larger format gap, and the holdout, which follows the train distribution, will not see it.

6) Spec gap: stale_pred.py:60 and holdout_eval.py:23 build SplitData without the view, so the stale and holdout replays of an HS1 checkpoint would silently use the full history.

Priors: P(same strength) about 0.4, P(member corr <= 0.92) about 0.03, P(pool margin >= 0.005) about 0.35. | fix: (a) Loader parity: store hist_src in ck['args'] and cfg, and apply src_history_view from the checkpoint, not from a CLI flag. This covers train.py (tr/va/te), finetune.py:125-134, stale_pred.py:60, holdout_eval.py:23 and every replay. Add a bit-exact check that each replay reproduces the stored val, holdout and test preds, as in HDROP-ALL.
(b) A pre-launch GPU probe of about 2 min with the HDROP replay harness. Apply the s1 view at inference to w5_e10_base_s951/952 and record the single-pass within-feed zcorr against the full-history replay, plus the change in val. Retraining moves the outputs back toward the base, so this zcorr is roughly a floor on the signal correlation a retrained HS1 can reach. Pre-declare: launch the 10-epoch pair only if the zcorr is <= 0.98; at >= 0.985 the expected pool margin is below 0.005, so close it without spending the training run.
(c) Fix the data facts in the pre-declaration: empty-slice share 2.97% val / 2.37% test / 2.87% train; s1-count PSI 0.217 train->val and 0.211 train->test (0.040 for the full H). Add the dead per-type columns (types <ids>, 8, 9, 10 carry no source) to the view test.
(d) State the expected outcome up front: member cross-corr about 0.93-0.94 (the 'material' <= 0.92 is not expected) and pool margin about 0.005-0.018. Keep the swap-pool clause (P) as the real arbiter. Also report margin / |member val delta| against the 4:1 frontier, as information only.
(e) Keep pre2_hmax32, ctx_nd_* and ctx_hn/hs at full history. Slicing them too would be a removal of load-bearing inputs (pre2 -0.0013, ctx_nd -0.0014), which falls below strength.

ranked.rule:
Pre-declare with `date -u` in nn_x/w5/logs/E_hs1_predeclared.txt before the first launch. Read on the selected checkpoint (@last is information only), paired per feed against w5_e10_base_s951/952.

KILL at step 60000: both seeds' holdout < base@60000 - 2*0.00077.

STAGE 1 = FAMILY CANDIDATE iff all of:
(S) pooled member val >= -0.0010 AND holdout >= -0.0005; no val slice (M<50, M>=50, Tue, Thu) < -2 SE; pmix >= -1 SE.
(D) diversity clause on val (div_readout.py mechanics): rho_bb - rho_x >= +0.005, where rho_bb = corr(base{951,952}, base{953,954}) = 0.97364 and rho_x = corr(hs1{951,952}, base{953,954}). Report the holdout margin and the member cross-corr against the 0.92 target; corr <= 0.92 is labelled 'material'.
(P) swap pool: z-mean{hs1_951, hs1_952, base_953, base_954} - z-mean{base_951..954} >= +0.0003 val AND >= 0 holdout.

STAGE 2 (new pre-declaration): seeds 953/954 + n2cpv3 FT x4, then decide7/9 with T = G3 + HS1(4), member-equal, 0.5 FT + 0.5 TO. PASS iff V >= +0.0005 AND H >= +0.0005, no slice < -2 SE, pmix >= -1 SE, presub_gate PASS. Pick 1 changes only under the frozen rule (H >= +2 SE vs G3 and V >= 0). Otherwise CLOSED, with a COVERAGE_MAP row.
ranked.cost: Code + tests: ~3 h CPU. Pair: 2 x ~60-75 min alone per GPU (shorter histories, likely ~0.8x of base step time), ~2.5 GPU-h including stale_pred, holdout preds and readout. Stage 2 if the pair passes: s953/954 ~2.5 GPU-h + 4 n2cpv3 FTs ~2 GPU-h + decide script on CPU. Total <= 7 GPU-h, about 1 day wall.
ranked.mechanism: Every member (TF, GRU, d192, every seed) builds its whole GPU-side history channel from the same 256 mixed-surface events. That channel is: cand x history cosine features (smax/smax8/smax32/lse/top3/per-type max), category-affinity counts, sim_bias, TabR top-16 retrieval and the history encoder. So all members share one history-driven component. HS1 rebuilds all of it from the s1 (recs-feed) events only, which are 33.8% of history events. The xt inputs (seq_cv, ctx_nd, ctx_hn/hs, pre2, LUO popularity) and user_emb stay as they are. The learned interactions then rank by similarity to what the user engaged with FROM THE FEED, the label's surface, and drop search-only interest. AUDIT_1112 §4.6: a category seen only via search has feed-click lift 0.91, vs 1.13 for feed-only. CPU check run now (scratchpad slicefeat.py, 3,946 val feeds): the s1-slice max-cos cue keeps almost all the ranking power (feed-macro AUC 0.636 vs 0.643 for the full history; the non-s1 slice gives 0.627). But it correlates only 0.85 (median 0.90) within feed with the full-history cue, and 0.66 with the complementary slice. So it is a different and nearly as informative view. The variant s1 + intent types keeps 79% of events at corr 0.93; that is too close, so it is rejected. Expected disagreement: candidates near recent SEARCH items but not near feed engagements are ranked up by the base and not by HS1, and vice versa.

ranked.name: CATGRAD: chain-rule ranker whose trunk learns only within-category contrasts, with a detached category factor
ranked.lens: error structure (RECAP_1113 §7: 58% of tail loss is within-category misordering, 66% sits in long feeds, and ~11 same-category items outrank the click)
reasons:
ok: No closed row uses the same mechanism, which is routing the CE_cat gradient away from the trunk and factorising the output as log P(cat) + log P(item|cat) with a detached category head. I checked these candidates:
(1) The N3 intent head, CLOSED as an old-recipe row in COVERAGE_MAP ("intent head, item-ID residual, position tower"). It is still in w5 as `--intent`: model.py lines 417-421 and 571-576, train.py lines 470-474. It uses the same L_c target (the share of positives per category), but the head reads the user token only. The trunk keeps the full CE plus the aux, and the head's output is added to the logit rather than replacing the trunk's LSE. Its result was -0.0014 val / +0.0003 holdout (nn_report:146). nn_report itself left "stop-gradient" untested.
(2) abl_wcat (CODES_EXPLOIT_1113 §4) is a spec only and was never run. It re-weights the loss on the same logits.
(3) The loss zoo (sol_solvers §2.1) used a frozen trunk, so it cannot show a change in the learned representation.
(4) FUTWIN/PFD ("category-intent family closed for good") was about adding new future information, not about gradient routing.
No leak: the head uses only candidate categories, counts and tokens. The spec is mechanically sound. For multi-positive y, the log-softmax of the composite equals log softmax(g)_k + h - LSE_k(h), so L_w + L_c is exactly listwise_loss on the composite. That makes FT and select_on=holdout work unchanged.

The strongest evidence against strength is not cited in the idea. err_category_intent §3-4: every dedicated category model (GBDT A/B/C, and the torch S1 with feed-composition features) is 0.0008-0.0025 category NDCG below the NN's own LSE. Category NDCG converts to item NDCG at about 0.85-0.9 (§5), which puts these models at roughly -0.0007..-0.002 item. In the nested decomposition, swapping in their category marginal always picked the smallest weight and still cost -0.0003..-0.0006 on nn_trainonly.
Mean-pooling is the specific weak point of the spec. In §2, mean aggregation of NN scores gives 0.693 category NDCG, max gives 0.752 and LSE gives 0.780. A head that sees only the category's mean token has to rebuild the "best sibling" signal on detached features that were never trained for category choice.
The mechanism is also only partial. K9 aux runs on the same trunk and distils production order across the whole feed, so cross-category gradient still reaches the trunk.

My priors: P(same strength, -0.0010 val / -0.0005 holdout) about 0.25-0.3 (the idea says 0.4). P(margin >= 0.005) about 0.25. P(member corr <= 0.92) about 0.04, which agrees with the idea. Even pop-free, the most decorrelated family measured (within-category corr 0.918, 2-epoch margin +0.0185), added only +0.00036 val to G3 (Q1a). G3 + family reaching >= +0.0005 on both val and holdout is therefore about 0.03. | fix: Amend before pre-declaring:
(a) Replace mean-pooling in cat_head with a pool that can carry the best sibling. Either use a learned-query softmax attention pool over the category's detached tokens (an LSE-like pool), or concat(mean, max). Keep log1p(count), since category size is 68% of the GBDT category gain. Reason: in err_category_intent §2, NN mean aggregation scores 0.693 category NDCG and LSE scores 0.780.
(b) Add a stage-S category-strength futility read. Compute category NDCG of softmax(g) against the base NN-LSE (0.78 scale), and the graft "CATGRAD category + base within". CLOSE if the graft is < -0.0006 val. This is the err_category_intent §3-4 failure mode, and it can be checked before any 10-epoch spend.
(c) Simplify train.py. L_w + L_c is exactly listwise_loss(composite, norm='feed'), because the composite's log-softmax is log softmax(g)_k + h - LSE_k(h). So only the model changes. CPU tests:
- that identity holds;
- for every (feed, category), the sum of dL/dh is 0, which is a direct proof that the trunk receives no CE_cat gradient;
- flag-off identity.
(d) State in the mechanism that K9 aux still sends cross-category production-order gradient into the trunk, so the "within-only trunk" is partial. Do not change K9, because it is the +0.0024 trunk regulariser.
(e) d1 uses a val bar of -0.0010, which is looser than the project's existing diversity clause (E_batch_predeclared amendment 1: val and holdout >= -0.0005). Either align it or write the deviation into the pre-declaration. Keep d3 (2-member pool >= -0.0005) as the binding strength check.
Expected cost unchanged: about 0.6 GPU-h for stage S and about 2.5 GPU-h for the 10-epoch pair.

ok: Not refuted. No closed row uses the same mechanism, I found no leak, and nothing in the record contradicts it. The core mechanism is untested: take CE_cat out of the shared trunk and model the output as log P(cat) + log P(item|cat). The algebra holds: CE on the composite equals L_c + L_w exactly. The per-(feed, category) candidate count is label-free and built the same way on train, val and test. Labels enter only the loss. But the design has four real weaknesses.

(1) The within-category gradient does not change. dCE_within/dh is the same function in both models. So any within-category decorrelation has to come second-hand, from the trunk representation changing once CE_cat is gone. That is the same class of change as removing a trunk supervision term. The nearest measured case is no_aux: 2-ep margin +0.0054, but strength -0.0022. Also, the K9 production-order aux still pushes cross-category gradient into the trunk, so the trunk does not learn 'only within-category contrasts'. The decorrelating lever is weaker than the name suggests.

(2) The category factor is the weak point, and the evidence offered for it does not carry over. Evidence (c)/(d) grafts category parts from families trained end to end, where the category part is the LSE of item logits. CATGRAD instead trains a separate category model on detached tokens. reports/err_category_intent.md §0 says:
- The NN's LSE category ranking (category NDCG 0.780) beats every dedicated category model: GBDT -0.0012 to -0.0025; a torch transformer with group features -0.0008; a history-only model -0.029.
- Mean aggregation of the NN's own scores gives 0.693, against 0.780 for LSE.
- Each unit of category NDCG converts to 0.83-0.92 units of item NDCG.
The spec's head is an MLP on MEAN-pooled detached tokens. Structurally that sits closer to mean aggregation than to LSE: it cannot express 'one sibling is a near-duplicate re-view'. Even at the best quality ever built (-0.0008 category NDCG), it would use most of the -0.0010 member budget before any within-category effect.

(3) Singleton categories are scored by g alone. I measured this on CPU (scratchpad singleton.py, val): 5.1% of positives sit in singleton categories and 10.6% in groups of size 2 or less. In M<50 feeds the singleton share is 13.3%, against 1.2% in M>=50. These positives are ranked purely by the detached head, which is a direct risk to the M<50 slice veto.

(4) Diversity from weakness is the default outcome. Every arm that reached the margin did so while losing strength: bs4 +0.0098 (member corr 0.936, val -0.0026), e30 +0.0066, bs4lr4 +0.0053. No measured arm has member corr <= 0.92. err_category_intent §4 also tested mixing the NN's category marginal with a dedicated category model ('swap'/'add', nested). The nested choice landed on the smallest weight, and the deltas ranged from -0.0008 to +0.0005, mostly <= 0. That is evidence against the category half of the claimed decorrelation adding pool value.

The proposer's priors are honest (P(corr <= 0.92) 0.04). My estimates: P(same strength) ~0.25-0.3 as specified, ~0.4 with the LSE fix; P(margin >= 0.005 | same strength) ~0.3; P(the pool moves >= +0.0005 on both val and holdout | both) ~0.3. That gives p_pool_gain ~0.03.

Spec nit: the train.py loss change is unnecessary. The existing listwise_loss on the composite logits already equals L_c + L_w with the correct gradients, and the detach alone keeps CE_cat out of the trunk. This also keeps FT and selection consistent. | fix: Amendments so the test isolates the claimed mechanism instead of a weak category head:

(a) Replace the mean-pooled category head with an LSE-shaped one: g_k = LSE over m in k of q(c_final.detach())_m, plus b(E2_k), plus lin1(log1p n_k). Here q is LN-Linear-GELU-Linear with a zero-init last layer; it may also take a linear term on the normalised X, so the head sees f3, popularity and the other inputs directly. This keeps the 'best sibling drives the category' behaviour (err_category_intent: LSE 0.780 vs mean 0.693 category NDCG). For a singleton, g_k reduces to its own q score.

(b) Drop the train.py loss change. Plain listwise_loss(composite, norm='feed') equals L_c + L_w exactly. The CPU test becomes two checks: the trunk gradient of CE(composite) equals the trunk gradient of L_w, and the head gradient equals that of L_c, to 1e-5, including singleton groups and padding. This cuts the code to model.py, about 3 h.

(c) Add pre-declared Stage-S PART gates, using the parts() decomposition already in scratchpad hybrid.py, paired per seed at the last checkpoint:
- (s4) category-head strength: composite(base within + catgrad category) minus base >= -0.0006 on val, and category NDCG of g vs base LSE >= -0.002. If either fails, the diversity comes from weakness: CLOSED.
- (s5) within-part strength: composite(base category + catgrad within) minus base >= -0.0008 on val, holdout >= -0.0005.
- Keep (s3) on the within-part corr.

(d) Report the M<50 slice at Stage S. 13.3% of M<50 positives sit in singleton categories, which only g scores. Apply the -2 SE slice veto already at the 2-ep screen.

(e) State in the spec that K9 still sends cross-category gradient into the trunk. An info-only number is the cross-seed corr of the between-category part, to show whether the decorrelation is coming from the head.

Everything else, including Stage E (d1)-(d3) and decide7 T1/T2, stands as written.
ranked.spec:
Code: one new helper nn_x/w5/cd_arms9.py, mirrored into nn_x/abl for the screen. Write-new + mv, off by default, AST proof and flag-off end-to-end identity as in waves 5-8.
(1) model.py: Ranker(catw=None), stored in cfg only when set. For catw='grad':
- O = one_hot(ccat, N_CAT) * cmask, shape [B,M,54].
- pooled = einsum('bmk,bmd->bkd', O, c_final.detach()) / O.sum(1).clamp_min(1).
- g = cat_head(pooled + E2.weight + lin1(log1p(O.sum(1)))) -> [B,54]. cat_head = LN-Linear-GELU-Linear with a zero-init last layer under extra_init. Mask absent categories to -1e4.

ranked.mechanism:
The softmax CE splits exactly into two parts: CE = CE_cat (which category gets the click) + CE_within (which sibling inside the category). On base951 val, after fitting a temperature, CE = 3.73 nats = 1.43 category + 2.30 within (62%). Training lowers the category part by 10% from uniform (1.59 to 1.43) but the within part by only 7.7% (2.49 to 2.30). Ordering inside a category is therefore the weak-signal, noise-dominated part of the problem. New CPU evidence (scratchpad decomp2.py, zoo10ep.py, zoo2ep.py, hybrid.py, hybrid2ep.py, cdarms.py):
(a) At 10 epochs the base seeds correlate 0.9485 overall, 0.960 on the between-category part and 0.940 on the within-category part. Every family that decorrelates does so only inside categories. Within / between correlations: pop-free 0.918 / 0.956, bs4 0.928 / 0.951, GRU 0.930 / 0.953, retr32u and blocks3 0.936 / 0.959. The 2-epoch ablation zoo and the cooldown-harness arms show the same pattern.
(b) Of the 4-seed ensemble gain (+0.00233 val), averaging only the within-category parts gives +0.0013; averaging only the between parts gives +0.00055.
(c) Chain-rule hybrids put every recipe change's strength loss inside the category. Grafting a family's within-category order onto the base's category choice costs: pop-free -0.0026, bs4 -0.0026, GRU -0.0015, no_set -0.0018, no_retr -0.0027, no_aux -0.0019. Grafting its category choice onto the base's within order costs between -0.0009 and +0.0003.
(d) G3 is calibrated by sibling rank (act/exp 0.96-1.04) and at category level (0.93-1.02). No new signal is left there, so a family can add value only through a different within-category bias.
In the base, the shared trunk takes both gradients, and category-level features (f3, recency, block mass) shape the representation that also orders siblings. CATGRAD removes CE_cat from the trunk. The trunk is supervised only by sibling contrasts (in tail feeds these are the hard negatives) plus the unchanged K9 aux. Category choice moves to a separate head on detached, pooled block tokens, so it is no longer the LSE of item logits. The final score is log P(cat) + log P(item|cat). The within-category features the trunk learns are therefore selected by a different gradient, which changes the error pattern where seed noise and tail loss are concentrated. The detached head also decorrelates the category part: swapping only the category part moved member corr by 0.0035-0.0075 at a cost of <= 0.0006.
Priors: P(member corr <= 0.92) ~0.04 (no measured family is below 0.935). p_decorrelated below = P(pool margin >= +0.005). P(G3 + family >= +0.0005 on both val and holdout) ~0.04.

ranked.name: JOINT: a single-stream transformer over [user; history; candidates] with feed-conditioned history and one shared softmax (replaces encode-then-cross-then-set)
ranked.lens: Architecture view of the same inputs: change the interaction topology. Every G3 member, transformer and GRU alike, encodes the history independently of the feed and then lets candidates read it. Here history tokens also attend to the shown candidates, and each candidate's attention mass is shared, in one softmax, between history evidence and the other candidates.
reasons:
ok: No closed row tests the same mechanism. Nothing in COVERAGE_MAP, TRICKS_SWEEP_1113 or EXPERIMENT_REGISTRY measures either of the two things the idea adds: history tokens attending to the shown feed, or one softmax shared by history keys and candidate keys. The near rows either change something else or were never run:
- nnx_research_recsys_arch §3.10 set aside "HSTU/LiGR/OneTrans unified stack, early fusion" because of cost. That was a design-stage call with no run behind it.
- EXTERNAL_TOP1 D3 (the model-5 clone) was never run, and it also changes the inputs and the loss.
- PRETRAIN_PLAN §5 closes HSTU/OneRec as pre-training, which is a different mechanism.
- r7 B5 block forms, hl2, diff2 and blocks3 keep the encode-then-cross topology.
- cset and typed change candidate-side retrieval and key masks, not the topology.
So this is an untested idea with a plausible mechanism, and it is not refuted.

The recorded facts do argue strongly against it succeeding:
(a) The closest measured change to how candidates read their context is cset. At 2 epochs its member correlation to the base was 0.9729 against base-base 0.9784, a margin of 0.0055, and it was promoted as a FAMILY-CANDIDATE. At 10 epochs the margin disappeared: arm-base cross 0.9370 against base-base 0.9365 (nn_x/r6/logs/r6_eval_e10_cset.txt). The 2-member mix was -0.00024 val. At 10 epochs, plateau iterate noise dominates the correlation, and wiring variants that keep the same inputs converge to the same function: GRU 0.0024, blocks3 0.0025, hl2 none.
(b) The cited precedent supports only mechanism (2). In Avito's model 5 (deep_ru_competitions H2), candidates attend to the history and to each other. OneTrans is causal with the sequence tokens first (nnx_research_recsys_arch.md:102-104), so its history never attends to the candidates. Its own ablation, "full instead of causal attention: +0.00%", is the nearest published measurement of mechanism (1), the feed-conditioned history, and it found nothing.
(c) Every 10-epoch arm that decorrelates is weaker. bs4 has margin +0.0098 but member -0.0026; e30 has +0.0066 but -0.0016; DIN's Δρ of 0.019 came at -0.0037. The r7 forms cost the M>=50 slice in 13/13 arms. Feed-size-sensitive attention puts the M>=50 slice at risk again.
(d) The idea's own arithmetic misses its goal. The fitted law it quotes, 0.8·(0.03·Δρ − 0.3·gap), gives at most +0.00036 for the expected Δρ of 0.006-0.015, even with zero gap. Reaching +0.0005 needs Δρ ≥ 0.021, about member corr ≤ 0.926. That sits above the top of the idea's own expected range.
(e) The tail is information-limited: positives lose on every cue, including cosine-to-history at 0.37. A different topology over the same cues is likely to make the same errors in the tail feeds that carry 66% of the loss.

The cost estimate of about 2-2.5x the base is plausible but slightly optimistic. Four joint layers over K+M ≈ 257+M tokens, with the FFN applied to every history token, cost about 3-4x the history-side compute. Expect 2.5-3.5 h per 10-epoch run alone on a GPU, about 6-7 GPU-h for the pair. This is not a reason to refute. | fix: Keep the idea, with five amendments to make it honest and testable:
1. **Split the two mechanisms with one boolean flag.** `--joint_hq 1` lets history and user queries attend to candidate keys (feed-conditioned history, the novel part, which has no strength precedent; OneTrans full attention measured +0.00%). `--joint_hq 0` blocks history-to-candidate keys, giving the model-5/OneTrans form, which has precedent. Pre-declare `joint_hq 1` as the decision arm. Add `joint_hq 0` to the 2-epoch screen only, so a strength failure can be attributed to one mechanism.
2. **Fix the softmax balance at init.**

In high-scale heads at init, history keys therefore get a +4 to +7 logit lead over candidate keys (bias 0), which suppresses the candidate-candidate path that the set attention's +0.0019 relies on.

   - Optional: also apply the cset cosine prior on the candidate-to-candidate block.

Change the screen to GO iff member val >= -0.0015, holdout >= -0.0010 and M>=50 >= -2 SE. Report the 2-epoch margin, but GO only if it is >= +0.010 (about 3x what cset had and lost); otherwise skip the 10-epoch pair.
4. **Align the 10-epoch rule with the goal.** By the quoted law, +0.0005 needs Δρ >= 0.021 at zero gap. Pre-declare STOP when member cross corr > 0.935 (not 0.940), and write the expected-gain line as 0.8·(0.03·Δρ − 0.3·gap) >= +0.0005 rather than +0.0003. Keep d1 at -0.0010, d3 at -0.0005, d4 slices and pmix, and the decide6 gate.
5. **Re-cost.** Assume 3-4x the history-side FLOPs, 2.5-3.5 h per 10-epoch run alone, about 6-7 GPU-h for the pair and about 15-17 GPU-h to a G3 decision. Under the 4-processes-per-GPU, >= 60 GB-free rule, run one joint run per GPU. The base already uses a float mask in the cross blocks, so memory is not the binding constraint.

ranked.mechanism:
Two information flows that no G3 member has:
(1) Feed-conditioned history. Which past events carry weight is re-computed per feed, so in a big feed with many same-category candidates the history events that discriminate among the shown items can dominate. 58% of the tail loss is within-category misordering in big feeds.
(2) Joint softmax competition between history keys (<= 257) and candidate keys (M up to 300). The balance between personal evidence and feed context shifts systematically with feed size, and feed size is the variable that determines the tail: M alone predicts a tail feed at AUC 0.766, and tail feeds carry 66% of val loss.
The errors should therefore move exactly where G3 loses, rather than being a weaker copy. Measured context from existing preds: history-encoder swaps (GRU, Δρ 0.0024) and capacity or width changes (blocks3 0.0025, retr32u 0.0026, d192 0.005) barely decorrelate, while the one interaction-mechanism change measured (DIN) reaches 0.019. JOINT changes the interaction topology, so the expected Δρ is about 0.006-0.015 at member level.

Our recipe uses the uniform-order portion only as a soft domain token and a 2% cooldown mix. Not in COVERAGE_MAP.
reasons:

The first is a factual error in the spec that will probably sink the strength leg. The second is recorded evidence that the decorrelation will be small.

(1) Same mechanism, already tested, but not binding. nn_report.md:64/81 pw_aux_sim used the same flag (--prand_base 0.2), the same per-feed weight prand_base + p and the same 1 - p aux weighting. The project has re-tested AdamW-era closures under Muon (d256 -> F12 d192), and it has judged strength-closed levers under the diversity clause (bs4, e20/e30, pop-free). So a diversity re-test is legitimate. It does mean the strength prior starts at about -0.001 at a 6x dose.

(2) The claim "keeps the m02 pool dose" is false in gradient terms. The up-weighted feeds are exactly the m02 pool: p > 0.5, M >= 50, holdout excluded, 134K feeds (train.py:398). The training log reports p_random mean 0.0570 including the holdout, which gives about 0.048 on the training feeds. With 0.3 + p normalised to mean 1, the pool feeds get about 3.6x weight and production feeds about 0.86x. The cooldown is 19,670 steps, i.e. 2 natural passes. The weighted dose on the pool feeds is then about 2 x 3.6 + 0.94 ≈ 8 pass-equivalents, about 19% of the cooldown gradient. The comparison points:
- base ≈ 2.9 pass-equivalents, about 6% of the gradient;
- m04 ≈ 3.9: STOP, val -0.00077, holdout -0.00046, coldpos z -3.45 (w5_eval_B_wave6.txt);
- mix 0.1 ≈ 6.7: end-minus-peak -0.0033 (r6_recap §3.3);
- mix 0.3: collapse.

The two scorings have within-feed corr 0.9982 and differ by +0.00011 ± 0.00017, a pure cold/warm trade. So the production-vs-random axis the model has learned is tiny. Removing the domain token (no_domain) is inconclusive: -0.00044 val / -0.00001 holdout (abl_eval.txt:244). The only measured reweighting arm, lnorm_batch, gave a margin of about 0.0023 at -0.0015. - pop1: pool V +0.0003 / H 0.0 (CURRENT_STATUS 06:39 and 09:22).

- P(member val >= -0.0010) about 0.25 as specified, about 0.4 with the fix below;
- P(margin >= 0.005) about 0.1;

ranked.mechanism:
Three parts of DIN (model.py _din) are a different function class from the transformer: (a) additive attention GELU(Wq c + Wk h)·w with a per-head cosine prior; (b) an un-normalised SiLU pooling channel, which carries how MANY history events match where softmax only gives a convex mixture; (c) a 2-layer DCNv2 over [c, soft, silu, user], i.e. explicit bounded-degree feature crosses. MEASURED on existing preds (CPU, read-only; scripts in /tmp/scratchpad/arch_div.py, din_mech.py):
- Member z-corr, same recipe (ii): F11 DIN vs F7 0.9212; GRU vs F7 0.9382, d192 0.9356, lr1e-3 0.9362; F7-F7 0.9406; DIN vs GRU 0.9183.
- Structural (infinite-pool) corr rho_x/sqrt(rho_aa rho_bb): DIN 0.9876 vs GRU 0.9971, d192 0.9992, lr1 0.9968. DIN's structural decorrelation is about 4x the GRU's. Of all measured arms only the pop-free family is higher (0.9834), and it pays 0.008 in holdout.
- Pool level, 4-member family vs 7-member F7 pool: DIN 0.9734 vs 0.985 for GRU/d192/lr1, about 0.988 expected for a same-recipe pool. That is a pool margin of about +0.014, and it passes the +0.005 clause. The GRU's margin is only about +0.003, so premise (3) is weak: the GRU family adds to G3 almost like extra seeds.
- The disagreement is uniform over feed size: corr(DIN, F7) 0.968-0.974 in every M bucket.
- Its sign on the cosine axis is opposite to the GRU's: DIN-F7 loads +0.06..+0.09 on cos_u / recent cosine, GRU-F7 loads -0.10. The two complement each other inside G3.

ranked.mechanism: 95.7% of training feeds are production feeds. All 20 G3 members (GRU and TF) learn their plateau on the same production-dominated mix and differ only by plateau iterate noise. PW re-weights the plateau's main listwise loss toward the 134K exploration feeds (R6 = exploration weight 6x production, about 20% of the plateau main-loss gradient instead of 4.3%). The plateau end-state sets member identity: re-cools of one root from @70k vs @77.5k correlate 0.976, against 0.948 across seeds (computed now). The cooldown (m02, K9 0.5->0.1) is left untouched, so the mechanism that supplies the whole gain does not change. Unlike pop-free and pop1, no input is removed. The nearby rows use different mechanisms. typed is a history-side mask by event type. retr_cat is history-side retrieval. no_set removes the set blocks entirely. xrel_more and the within-category input families (AUDIT_1112) are input-side. cset is a soft, learnable cosine prior in the same set blocks plus candidate kNN retrieval; the model can scale that prior down, but it cannot undo a hard mask.

The proposal's evidence (c) is overstated, though. It cites cset's 2-epoch margin (+0.0055) and says cset "stayed same-strength at 10 epochs", but leaves out cset's 10-epoch diversity: there was none. Uniform attention within a category would give about 0.67-0.69 at M=100-147. So CATCTX is not a near-copy, which helps the diversity prior. But it removes a pooling the base learned to use, which hurts the strength prior.

ranked.mechanism:
In the base, the two candidate-set attention blocks mix all ~109 candidates of a long feed. A candidate's standing among its siblings is therefore computed against a feed-wide context dominated by other categories. CATCTX masks every set block to same-category siblings, plus self. Each candidate is compared only with its real competitors, and cross-category choice comes from the softmax over the blocks' item logits and from history attention.
Why this targets the error pattern (CPU evidence, scratchpad):
(a) All family decorrelation and the larger share of ensemble gain live inside categories: base-base within 0.940 vs between 0.960; within-only averaging gives +0.0013 of the +0.0023 4-seed gain.
(b) The set attention's value is almost entirely within-category. Removing it (no_set, 2 ep) costs -0.00178 in the within part and only -0.00028 in category choice (hybrid2ep.py). Re-framing that context therefore changes the component that matters.
(c) Candidate-context changes are the largest same-strength decorrelators seen. The r6 cset arm (candidate-kNN set context) had cross corr 0.9729 vs 0.9784 base-base at 2 ep; no_set had a 2-ep margin of +0.0035, of which within +0.0031. Loss or weight changes move the function far less (K9-dose re-cools 0.997-0.999 same-root corr; lnorm_batch +0.0016).
(d) The history-side alternative would be a near-copy: within (feed, category) groups, max cosine to same-category history correlates 0.983 with max cosine to the full history (cathist.py). So the re-framing is placed on the candidate side.
Priors: P(member corr <= 0.92) ~0.06. p_decorrelated below = P(pool margin >= +0.005). P(G3 + family >= +0.0005 on both val and holdout) ~0.05.
